title: Green synthesis and characterization of CuO PANI nanocomposite for efficient Pb (II) adsorption from contaminated water

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the survey spectra showed the presence of 'Cu1s, O1s, C1s, and N1s' using a Thermo K-alpha with Al anode. Cu 1s has a binding energy around 8979 eV, which cannot be excited by Al Kα X-rays (1486.6 eV); the observed copper signal would be Cu 2p/Cu 3p, not Cu 1s.

predicted_errors.error_location: XRD results, g-CuO NPs hkl assignments
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text assigns the peaks at 49° and 58° both to the hkl 202: 'higher 2θ values (32, 49, 53, 58, 61, and 68°) which corresponding to the hkl (110, 202, 020, 202, 022, -202) planes respectively'. The same hkl cannot correspond to two different 2θ peaks; for monoclinic CuO these are typically (-202) and (202).

predicted_errors.error_location: XRD results, g-CuO NPs peak list
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says the two characteristic peaks at 35° and 38° are accompanied by 'multiple smaller peaks at higher 2θ values (32, 49, 53, 58, 61, and 68°)'. However, 32° is lower than 35° and 38°, so it cannot be described as a higher 2θ value.

The text states 'the morphology of nanocomposite after Pb (II) adsorption is depicted in Fig. 4 (c)', but the SEM/EDS discussion otherwise uses Fig. 3(a), 3(b), and 3(c). The after-adsorption SEM panel should be Fig. 3(c), not Fig. 4(c).

The pH study states 'initial ion concentration of 25 mg/L, and a CuO/PANI dosage of 25 mg/L'. In the Methods, 100 mL of Pb(II) solution was treated with 25 mg of CuO/PANI, which corresponds to 250 mg/L, not 25 mg/L. The unit/value is inconsistent.

The text first reports Pb(II) peaks at 139.25 and 144.14 eV assigned to Pb 4f7/2 and Pb 4f5/2. It then states 'Pb⁴⁺ is responsible for the binding energy peaks at 141.08 eV and 138.43 eV, while Pb (II) is at 138.69 eV and 143.78 eV'. These two Pb(II) assignments contradict each other, and the Pb(IV) assignment is inconsistent with the preceding spectrum description.

Before adsorption, N1s peaks are reported at 399.83 and 401.32 eV. After adsorption, the text says the survey scan shows 'N1s (401.60 eV to 399.83 eV)', implying a pre-adsorption value of 401.60 eV that was not reported earlier.

The text assigns 'peaks at 1562 and 1412 cm⁻¹' to 'PANI's N-H and C=N stretching, respectively'. N-H stretching is normally observed around 3200-3500 cm⁻¹, not at 1562 cm⁻¹; the 1562 cm⁻¹ band is typically a ring/quinonoid C=C mode.
The plant is repeatedly called 'Haldinia cordifolia', but the accepted botanical name is Haldina cordifolia (formerly Adina cordifolia). 'Haldinia' is an invalid genus spelling.

The text states: 'When the pH rises above 6, lead ions precipitate as hydroxides, and removal efficiency decreases.' If Pb precipitates as Pb(OH)2, total Pb removal from the aqueous phase generally increases or becomes dominated by precipitation; the claim that removal efficiency decreases is chemically questionable and unsupported by the shown data.
